closed_r2_findings.closure_evidence: workflow-selftest.yml lines 99 and 195 both read `uses: ./.github/workflows/policy-check.yml@f2a674ba28a6f0b9a344f14568f5d1912c9351fa`. The two PIN comments (lines 97–98, 193–194) are updated to the same SHA. The validate-selftest-config preflight pin-equality check will pass; the callee at that SHA declares fixture-path so the reusable-workflow call will not error.

workflow-selftest.yml line 202: `if: always()` is present on the workflow-selftest job. Lines 228–245 assert FIXTURE_PASS_STASH_RESULT == 'success' and FIXTURE_FAIL_RESULT ∈ {success, failure} before the comparison step runs, so the harness always executes and always inspects the fixture-fail outcome regardless of its exit code.

workflow-selftest.yml lines 305–317: explicit exit-code assertion added. `fixture_fail_result = os.environ['FIXTURE_FAIL_RESULT']`; `fixture_fail_has_deny = any(item.get('verdict')=='deny' for item in actual_by_case['fixture-fail']['findings'])`. Asserts deny→result=='failure' and no-deny→result=='success'. This couples threshold-enforcement behaviour directly to the oracle comparison chain.

docs/plans/WP-SCP-020-policy-federation-primitive.md §4 020B.1 row (line 109) now lists four trigger paths including `schemas/policy-check-summary.schema.json` with the rationale '(expected-annotations.json is schema-bound; schema changes must re-validate all fixture expectations; blocks merge of any PR touching those paths)'. Matches the four-path workflow-selftest.yml trigger block lines 5–9.

docs/plans/WP-SCP-020-policy-federation-primitive.md §4 020B AC (i) (line 108) now enumerates fixture-path as a seventh input: 'fixture-path: string (default: ".") — restricts changed-file discovery to a path prefix; defaults to whole-repo evaluation for normal callers; used by the selftest harness for fixture-tree isolation'. Implementation at policy-check.yml lines 37–40 is now plan-aligned.

findings.claim: tests/workflow/** is absent from the plan §4 020K CODEOWNERS path list. The oracle files fixture-pass/expected-annotations.json and fixture-fail/expected-annotations.json will carry live deny findings after 020C but have no designated-reviewer gate at PR time until CODEOWNERS lands in 020K.
findings.evidence: docs/plans/WP-SCP-020-policy-federation-primitive.md §4 020K (line 114): CODEOWNERS path list enumerates 'policies/**, renovate/**, .github/workflows/**, docs/DECISIONS.md, output/findings/waivers.json' — five paths, tests/workflow/** absent. The gap was first raised as R2-CMP-MIN-01 (completeness lens) and R2-SBP-MIN-04 (safety lens) in round 2; neither has been acted on. conftest.md does not warn the 020C author that the oracle will be unguarded until 020K.
findings.impact: From 020C merge (when fixture-fail/expected-annotations.json carries real deny findings) until 020K merge, any push-access holder can stage a two-PR attack — PR-A changes only services.yml, PR-B changes only expected-annotations.json — bypassing the same-PR ratchet without a reviewer gate. The window spans slices 020C through 020J. After 020K the attack requires CODEOWNERS approval of both PRs, but only if tests/workflow/** is in the CODEOWNERS list; if it is not, the 020K deliverable will not close this gap.
findings.mitigation: (1) Amend plan §4 020K CODEOWNERS path list to add 'tests/workflow/** — oracle files for the selftest harness; mutations require named-reviewer sign-off.' (2) Add one sentence to conftest.md: 'tests/workflow/** will be covered by CODEOWNERS in slice 020K; until that slice merges, oracle file changes require manual review discipline.' Both edits can be batched into the same commit. Must land before 020C dispatch opens.

findings.claim: The field waiver_ref: W-020B1-SELFTEST in tests/workflow/fixture-fail/services.yml is not defined in the SVC-003 accepted_modes schema, not documented in conftest.md, and has no corresponding waivers document in the repository. If SCP-R-001 (020C) validates accepted_modes entries with additionalProperties: false, this field will produce an unexpected deny finding on an unknown-field path rather than on the intended mode.bearer_legacy + out-of-range deprecation_close_date path, making the 020C transition require a fixture edit rather than an oracle-only flip.
findings.evidence: tests/workflow/fixture-fail/services.yml lines 14–17: accepted_modes entry is {mode: mode.bearer_legacy, deprecation_close_date: '2099-12-31', waiver_ref: W-020B1-SELFTEST}. docs/plans/WP-SCP-020-policy-federation-primitive.md §4 020C: SCP-R-001 validates 'services.yml root-shape conformance to pre-D-021 SVC-003 mode set' and lists mode, deprecation_close_date; waiver_ref is not enumerated. No waivers.json or DECISIONS.md entry references W-020B1-SELFTEST. conftest.md (all 17 lines) does not mention waiver_ref. Raised as R2-CMP-MIN-02 in round 2; unaddressed.
findings.impact: If SCP-R-001 uses strict schema validation, fixture-fail fails for the wrong reason after 020C, and the 020C plan (oracle-only flip) is invalidated. The pre-positioned forward-reference to W-020B1-SELFTEST also creates a false impression that a waiver exists for this fixture service, which could mislead future readers of the file.
findings.mitigation: Option A (preferred): remove waiver_ref from fixture-fail/services.yml and add a YAML comment '# mode.bearer_legacy with deprecation_close_date 2099-12-31 intentionally out of range: SCP-R-001 will deny this once 020C ships'. Option B: confirm in conftest.md and the 020C dispatch package that SCP-R-001 does not validate waiver_ref (mode-entry-level, rule only checks mode and deprecation_close_date). If Option B, add the confirmation note to conftest.md explicitly. Must resolve before 020C dispatch opens.

findings.claim: The fixture-path input description in policy-check.yml still reads 'Restrict changed-file discovery to a fixture subtree when the selftest harness invokes the workflow', framing this as a harness-only feature. The input is general-purpose and usable by any caller for monorepo subdirectory scoping; the harness-only framing will prevent adopters from discovering the capability when reading ADOPT-001 §12 (020H part 3).
findings.evidence: policy-check.yml line 38: description: 'Restrict changed-file discovery to a fixture subtree when the selftest harness invokes the workflow.' The validation logic at lines 190–215 is fully general: any non-empty, control-character-free relative path is accepted. The plan §4 020B AC(i) now documents fixture-path correctly (fix-round-2 closure of R2-CMP-MAJ-02) but the in-file description still says 'selftest harness'. Raised as R2-CMP-nit-01 in round 2; unaddressed.
findings.impact: No runtime regression. An adopter wanting to scope policy evaluation to a monorepo package subdirectory would not discover this capability from the input description and may duplicate logic or file a feature request for functionality that already exists.
findings.mitigation: Update policy-check.yml line 38 description to: 'Restrict changed-file discovery to a path prefix. Defaults to "." (whole-repository evaluation). Set to a fixture directory when invoking from a test harness, or to a subdirectory to scope evaluation to a monorepo package.'

findings.claim: conftest.md documents the ratchet rule ('Existing fixture pairs are ratcheted: a PR may not change both services.yml and expected-annotations.json for the same committed fixture in one change') but does not call out the new-pair exception: a pair being introduced for the first time may include both files in one PR because exists_at(base, …) returns false for both.
findings.evidence: workflow-selftest.yml lines 73–89: ratchet condition gates on exists_at(base, services_path) AND exists_at(base, expected_path); new pairs have neither file at base so the ratchet is bypassed entirely. conftest.md lines 11–16 document the ratchet behaviour but contain no mention of this exception. Raised as R2-CMP-nit-02 in round 2; unaddressed.
findings.impact: Very low. Design-correct behaviour for bootstrapping new fixtures. A future contributor introducing a low-quality new fixture pair with a trivially-passing oracle would not be warned that the pair starts unratcheted, and a reviewer who expects the ratchet to protect new pairs would be surprised.
findings.mitigation: Add one sentence to conftest.md after the ratchet description: 'New fixture pairs introduced for the first time may include both files in one PR; the ratchet applies only to pairs that already exist at the PR base.'

findings.claim: The plan document version header was not bumped after the fix-round-2 amendments. The header still reads 'Version: 0.6 (FIXPOINT at round 5; §14 unknowns resolved 2026-04-21)' even though §4 020B AC(i) and §4 020B.1 were materially amended (fixture-path input added; schemas/policy-check-summary.schema.json trigger added). findings.evidence: docs/plans/WP-SCP-020-policy-federation-primitive.md line 6: '**Version:** 0.6 (FIXPOINT at round 5; §14 unknowns resolved 2026-04-21 — see `plan-fixpoint-log.md`)'. Two substantive §4 rows were edited in fix-round-2 (commit 169c485 references 'close 5 R2 MAJ findings (selftest pin + threshold + plan)'). No version bump or plan-fixpoint-log.md amendment is visible. The delta is governance-important: post-fixpoint plan amendments should be traceable.
findings.impact: Low. No implementation consequence. Future auditors comparing the plan to implementation may not immediately recognise that the plan was amended post-fixpoint, and may not know to consult R2/R3 review evidence to understand when and why. The fixpoint-log gap is the more significant sub-issue.
